primary_check.stored_primary_model: ordered logit (BIC did not confirm the partial proportional-odds model)

actor_attribution.source_rule: Attribution follows the final labels' source: the coders' majority for human-coded narratives (validation batch 1 and adjudication batch 2), the reference-run attribution for automated narratives. A record enters the cross-tabulation only when its final cue is 1.
actor_attribution.split_rule: rider-attributed = rider or both; driver-attributed = driver or both; unclear-attributed = unclear, or cue positive with no attribution recorded (prespec section 8b)

actor_recorded_but_cue_zero.note: Human-coded records where at least one coder recorded an attribution but the majority cue is 0. They are not cue-positive and are excluded from the cross-tabulation and the indicators.

coder_ties.note: build_final_labels.py resolves a tied attribution by the first most frequent value. The tie is listed so the reader can see which records carry an arbitrary attribution.

validation_agreement_llm_vs_coders.note: Agreement is computed on narratives where the coders' majority codes the cue positive with a non-tied attribution and the reference run codes the cue positive. Batch 1 is the validation sample; batch 2 is the flagged adjudication set, selected for disagreement and not a random sample. Agreement is unweighted (validation_metrics.py also reports inverse-probability-weighted label metrics; these are not). Kappa is uninformative where either side uses one level only, e.g. signal_violation in batch 2, where the coders used only 'rider'.

actor_attribution.disposition: descriptive cross-tabulation only: at least one resulting indicator falls below the 10-event rule in a severity class, so under prespec section 8b the split does not enter M1 and no split model is estimated

unknown_ethnicity.unknown_recode: unknown = Prsn_Ethnicity_ID recorded Unknown or missing; other = Asian, Other, American Indian

alcohol_test.code_note: raw CRIS codes; no code lookup is held in the repository, so meanings are not attached here

drug_test.code_note: raw CRIS codes; 97 is the most frequent code; no lookup is held in the repository

text_counts.rider_age_quantile_method: numpy.percentile, linear interpolation; unknown ages excluded

settings.pooling: Rubin's rules; total variance W + (1 + 1/m) B; t intervals with Barnard-Rubin degrees of freedom; complete-data df 488 (n minus parameters)

imputation_models.rider_age: predictive mean matching, 5 donors, on a Bayesian linear regression draw (rider_age, years)
imputation_models.posted_speed_limit: predictive mean matching, 5 donors, on a Bayesian linear regression draw (Crash_Speed_Limit; -1 and missing treated as missing), so imputed values are posted limits that occur in the data
imputation_models.gender: binary logit (female vs male), ridge 0.1 on slopes, parameters drawn from the normal approximation; Unknown and missing treated as missing
imputation_models.ethnicity: multinomial logit over white, black, hispanic, other (Asian, other, American Indian), ridge 0.1 on slopes, parameters drawn from the normal approximation; Unknown and missing treated as missing
imputation_models.predictors_cross: each model also uses the current values of the other three imputed fields (age and speed standardized, female, ethnicity dummies)
imputation_models.initialization: random draws from the observed values

band_coding.age: under 25; 25 to 54 (ref); 45 and over (threshold of the primary)
band_coding.ethnicity: white (ref); black; hispanic; other. With unknown imputed, the primary's other-or-unknown level becomes other alone. It is kept as its own level although it fails the 10-event rule, because section 4 offers no other merge and pooling it into White is not permitted.

multiple_imputation.mar_caveat: Imputation assumes the fields are missing at random given the predictors, including severity. The three person-field unknowns co-occur and concentrate in the O class, which is the pattern expected if reporting completeness depends on the injury itself; conditioning on severity carries that dependence into the imputation, but missingness that depends on the unrecorded value itself is not repaired.

spatial_indicator.prespec_indicator: prespec section 2.1 'Urbanized': 1 if the crash point falls inside a 2020 Census Urban Area of population 200,000 or more, city lookup where coordinates are absent. It is not in model_frame.csv and was not among the screened candidates; it is built here from tl_2020_us_uac20 and ua_list_all.txt.
spatial_indicator.note_rural_fl: Rural_Fl is the CRIS rural flag, complete for all rows; Rural_Urban_Type_ID is missing for 415 of 522 rows and cannot carry a split.

covariates_dropped.speed_unknown: rural: smallest cell 0; non_rural: smallest cell 2
covariates_dropped.gender_unknown: rural: smallest cell 0; non_rural: smallest cell 3
covariates_dropped.age_unknown: rural: smallest cell 1; non_rural: smallest cell 4
covariates_dropped.coord_missing: rural: smallest cell 0; non_rural: smallest cell 3

rural_vs_nonrural_test.note: The bootstrap p-value governs. The asymptotic reference assumes a sample size this design does not have, and where the two disagree the asymptotic one is the optimistic one.
rural_vs_nonrural_test.function: transferability.temporal_test on a 0/1 split column (replications 500, seed 20260914, subsample minimum cell 5)

urbanized_area_indicator.city_lookup_rule: a record without coordinates takes 1 if at least half the located records of its City_ID fall inside a qualifying urban area; 'Not Listed' or a city with no located record falls back to the CRIS rural flag

covariates_dropped.speed_unknown: inside_ua200k: smallest cell 0; outside_ua200k: smallest cell 0
covariates_dropped.gender_unknown: inside_ua200k: smallest cell 2; outside_ua200k: smallest cell 1
covariates_dropped.age_unknown: inside_ua200k: smallest cell 3; outside_ua200k: smallest cell 2
covariates_dropped.coord_missing: inside_ua200k: smallest cell 2; outside_ua200k: smallest cell 1
covariates_dropped.urban_area_200k: inside_ua200k: smallest cell 60; outside_ua200k: smallest cell 15

ua200k_test.note: The bootstrap p-value governs. The asymptotic reference assumes a sample size this design does not have, and where the two disagree the asymptotic one is the optimistic one.
ua200k_test.function: transferability.temporal_test on a 0/1 split column (replications 500, seed 20260914, subsample minimum cell 5)
ua200k_test.mask_note: first side (the split mask) is inside the urban areas

three_way.rule: six major cities = City_ID in Austin, Houston, San Antonio, Dallas, Fort Worth, El Paso, taking precedence; rural = CRIS Rural_Fl Y among the rest; other urban = the remainder
